question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III) is running a Convertible Arbitrage on a company's 10% convertible bond. Which position set describes the classic convertible arbitrage?

answer.text: Long the convertible bond + long the underlying equity
Short the convertible bond + short the underlying equity
Long the convertible bond + short the underlying equity
Long the equity + short an at-the-money put on the convertible

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 10.1.3, convertible arb is long the convertible security and SHORT the issuer's equity. The fund earns coupon + captures mispricing in conversion option; equity short hedges delta of the embedded call. **The Trap:** A and B mis-sign the hedge leg; D invents an exotic position not described in the chapter. The chapter uses a clean long-convertible / short-equity pair. **Cross-Exam Context:** VIII (Equity Derivatives) explains the embedded option valuation. XIX-C covers the same strategy as part of all-category manager syllabus. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Delta-hedge ratio = N(d1) * conversion ratio. Re-hedge when realized delta drifts 10% from model delta; each re-hedge costs borrow fee (often 50-200 bps p.a.) which erodes the risk-free arb claim — size by net carry, not headline spread.
